item.title: Trump faces tough choices as Iran dangles deal to reopen Hormuz before US midterms
item.description:
Iran’s seven-day timetable would restart nuclear talks, but will the US be willing to deliver on terms that include reining in Israel in Lebanon?

Iran’s seven-day timetable to reopen the strait of Hormuz and start talks on its nuclear programme has been pitched as a deal that could rapidly extricate Donald Trump from a political crisis but requires the US president to make difficult concessions.

In the five days left before the proposed reopening of the strait, which is expected to relieve pressure on global energy markets, Trump would need to lift Iranian asset freezes, permit Iran to export its oil and, probably most difficult of all, order Benjamin Netanyahu to end Israel’s attacks on Hezbollah in Lebanon, thus achieving the “ceasefire on all fronts”.

item.title: Backlash as Indian oil heir made professor of sustainability by Newcastle University
item.description:
Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity

Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.

The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.

item.title: Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports
item.description:
Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports

Parents across Riyadh received emails from schools on Sunday announcing a last-minute plan to shift to remote learning for a week, according to messages seen by AFP.

"We have just been informed by Saudi authorities that schools must remain closed all week," read two separate messages seen by AFP. 

There was no official reason given but the move comes amid heightened tensions in the Gulf and near-daily attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia by the Houthi fighters in Yemen.

"When a decision affects an entire school community for a full week, families deserve clear communication and transparency about the reasons behind it," one parent living in Riyadh who spoke on condition of anonymity told AFP. 

"It's a last-minute decision. We have no clue what's happening," a Lebanese expatriate living in Riyadh added.

The announcement comes a day after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles targeting the kingdom. 

The strikes were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks since July, when renewed hostilities shattered a years-long truce and embroiled Yemen in the wider Middle East war.

The United Nations Security Council earlier condemned escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi fighters, noting that the strikes have wounded "civilians, including women and children".

Report by AFP

item.title: Saudi Arabia calls for 'comprehensive' regional navigation security
item.description:
Saudi Arabia calls for 'comprehensive' regional navigation security

Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan used his address at the UN General Assembly to call for serious international cooperation to protect freedom of navigation and stress that a regional security framework should be "comprehensive".

“Protecting international navigation is a shared responsibility that requires serious international cooperation,” he said.

Prince Faisal, who led the Saudi delegation at the UNGA, added that Riyadh supports efforts to reduce tensions in the region and stressed that "any arrangements for its security be comprehensive".

He also supported initiatives aimed at de-escalation, particularly efforts by Qatar and Pakistan, saying they can help restore regional stability. 

The minister accused Iran of flagrant attacks on civilian and economic targets across the region, while calling on the international community to condemn Houthi actions threatening Red Sea shipping.
